findings.label: Backend endpoint assumption
findings.description: The implementation calls `/api/v1/wallet/deposit/cancel` and `/api/v1/wallet/deposit/fail` in the callback handlers, but these endpoints are not verified to exist in the codebase. Confirm these routes are implemented on the backend.

findings.label: Missing reference parameter in cancel endpoint
findings.description: The `onCancel` handler sends `reference` in the request body to `/api/v1/wallet/deposit/cancel`, but does not construct the URL with a path parameter. Verify the backend endpoint signature matches (`POST /api/v1/wallet/deposit/cancel` with reference in body, not a path parameter like `/api/v1/wallet/deposit/{reference}/cancel`).

findings.label: Fail endpoint reference handling
findings.description: The `onError` handler calls `/api/v1/wallet/deposit/fail` with `reference` in the body. Confirm this endpoint signature matches what the backend expects.

findings.label: Silent error handling in callbacks
findings.description: If the backend cancel/fail calls fail, the error is logged but a success alert is still shown to the user immediately. This could mask backend state mismatches. Consider showing the alert only after the backend call completes successfully, or adding a user-facing warning if the backend call fails.
